premises.reasoning: No intent signal against it: the operator kept status rows in keyboard navigation (journal.md:24), which makes them focus targets, and the plan promises a keyboard-operable WAI-ARIA tree (plan.md:49, AC5). Row ids change per state (MetaprojectTree.tsx:33,37,46,47) and nothing restores focus (:124-135 only acts on focusRequest set by moveTo :155-159). WAI-ARIA APG tree pattern expects focus to stay on a treeitem. Fix keeps the system consistent.

The plan chose to re-read expanded folders on a new snapshot (plan.md:53) but not to fan them out unbounded; the 8-permit fail-fast in metaproject.rs:186-199 predates the branch (904fd138a) and answers 'Retry shortly', which the tree turns into terminal folder errors (useMetaprojectTree.ts read/catch). Read latency and cancellation are out of scope (description.md:29), so only the non-cancellation tail of the impact is out of scope; the burst-failure core is a correctness outcome, not latency. Overlaps performance-w1-F-002 (same site).

Contradicts the stated intent rather than following it: plan.md:49 'Focus is never moved by data arriving' and AC6 'without moving focus' (acceptance-criteria.md:8). moveTo (MetaprojectTree.tsx:155-159) leaves focusRequest pending when setFocusId is a no-op (Home on first / End on last row), and the dependency-free layout effect (:131-134) consumes it on the next unrelated commit. No signal of a deliberate choice.

The group-key rule is part of the tree contract the plan publishes (plan.md:18, 'other' for pages without a type), yet core keeps it private (metaproject-explorer-v2.ts:33,145) and Desktop hand-copies it with || (MetaprojectTree.tsx:58). Single-source practice supports a shared export; the fix makes the two sides more consistent. Duplicate of architecture-w2-F-001.

Same premise as architecture-w1-F-001: contract rule (plan.md:18) duplicated between metaproject-explorer-v2.ts:33/145 and MetaprojectTree.tsx:58 with ?? vs ||. No intent signal for keeping it unexported.

negotiateMetaproject (platform/metaproject.ts:277) is now called only from metaproject.test.ts while the view uses negotiateMetaprojectExplorer (journal.md:21). No comment or exemption marks it as a deliberate alias; removing the duplicate entry point is ordinary practice.

For the production transport the check at useMetaprojectTree.ts:124 cannot fire: requestMetaprojectV2 -> matchesRequest (platform/metaproject.ts:311) already throws a generic 'Choose the bundled CLI' error on a snapshot mismatch, so the hook comment (:66) misstates the stale path. The hook takes `request` as an injectable dependency, so the guard is reachable with a fake; this interacts with testing-practices-w1-F3, and the finding's second fix option (matchesRequest throws stale-snapshot) satisfies both findings consistently.
AC5 lists Up (acceptance-criteria.md:7) and the docs key table documents it; a missing test of a criterion key is a test gap that stays as reported. Duplicate of testing-practices-w1-F4.

premises.question: Reveal pages sequentially by design and latency is out of scope here. Dismiss and track it in the read-latency stage, or keep it as a finding for this PR?
options: dismiss - track in the read-latency stage
uphold - change reveal in this PR

premises.reasoning: Same premise as highload-w1-F-001 at the same site (MetaprojectTree.tsx:97, useMetaprojectTree.ts read): unbounded re-read fan-out after a snapshot change. Plan.md:53 chose the re-read, not its concurrency; no bound or intent signal exists.

groups.set(key, [...groups.get(key) ?? [], node]) at metaproject-explorer-v2.ts:146 copies the array per page; no intent signal, and push-in-place is the idiomatic equivalent with identical output. Minor as reported.

The PR changed Desktop from requiring every action to requiring METAPROJECT_REQUIRED_ACTIONS (platform/metaproject.ts:167-180) and its own new guide text says an older CLI keeps the flat list (desktop-metaproject.md:132), while desktop-metaproject.md:309 and :332 still say Desktop needs every action it uses. Docs contradicting the shipped behaviour; AC9 covers the guide. docs/docs/cli-reference.md carries the same sentence.
A negative assertion over a model that never contains symbols does not test AC1's 'never symbols' (acceptance-criteria.md:3). Test gaps stay as reported; no intent or practice source shrinks it.
AC1 requires sorted children (acceptance-criteria.md:3); pre-sorted fixtures cannot detect a removed comparator. A test-strength gap, upheld.

AC6 requires dropping stale answers (acceptance-criteria.md:8); the fakes always answer the expected snapshot, so onStale is unpinned. Upheld; see degradation-w1-F-002 for the interaction on the snapshot-mismatch branch.
AC5 lists Up (acceptance-criteria.md:7) and no test presses ArrowUp. Upheld; duplicate of frontend-w2-F-001.
Empty built-graph and empty-wiki states render distinct text (MetaprojectTree.tsx:204-207) and the core not-found guard is unpinned; a test gap with a concrete regression path. Upheld.
A focus test that never proves the data arrived can pass vacuously; the plan's 'Focus is never moved by data arriving' (plan.md:49) is the behaviour it should pin. Upheld.
The operator chose to reveal only user selections (journal.md:24); the test pins that only negatively and cannot distinguish 'no default selection'. Upheld.

The operator kept status rows in keyboard navigation (journal.md:24); the finding accepts that and targets the focus loss when those rows change key (MetaprojectTree.tsx:33-47, 222-238). WCAG 2.4.3 and the WAI-ARIA APG tree pattern support it. Overlaps frontend-w1-F-001.

The loading row is a live region (MetaprojectTree.tsx:222) but the error row replacing it is not (:226-229), so a failure is silent to screen readers; WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages. The operator's wording choice (journal.md:24) concerns text, not announcement. Upheld.

The nav's aria-label 'Search results' (MetaprojectView.tsx:918) predates the PR, but this PR puts the tree inside it without a query, so the name now disagrees with the visible 'Files'/'Wiki' heading (plan.md:55). The operator's 'wording as implemented' (journal.md:24) covered the tree's strings, not this landmark name. WCAG 2.4.6 / 1.3.1. Upheld.

The operator kept the module-folder key behaviour (journal.md:24) and the finding keeps it; it asks only for a visual cue, which plan.md:50 neither specifies nor rules out. Nielsen #4/#6 support a cue; node rows already show a kind label (MetaprojectTree.tsx:247), so the fix is consistent with siblings.
